nodes.description: Biallelic KASH5 variants remove the protein or keep it out of the nuclear envelope. A homozygous frameshift abolishes KASH5 in the patient's testis. The missense p.Leu197Pro in the coiled-coil domain blocks nuclear envelope distribution of KASH5 and with it the nuclear-envelope enrichment of its partner SUN1. The transmembrane-domain variant p.Leu535Gln misroutes KASH5 to mitochondria in cultured cells, and a splice-site variant reported in women with ovarian insufficiency weakens nuclear envelope localization and SUN1 binding. Splice-site variants found in a man with meiotic arrest cause exon skipping in minigene assays.

nodes.description: In meiotic prophase I, telomeres attach to the inner nuclear membrane through SUN1, and KASH5 links SUN1 across the envelope to cytoplasmic dynein, for which it is an activating adaptor; KASH5 also binds the kinesin KIF5B. In Kash5-null mouse spermatocytes telomeres still attach to the envelope, but they are no longer coupled to the microtubule motors that move them and cluster them into the meiotic bouquet.
nodes.id: Uncoupling of Meiotic Telomeres from Cytoplasmic Dynein

evidence.reference_title: A conserved KASH domain protein associates with telomeres, SUN1, and dynactin during mammalian meiosis.
evidence.snippet: These results suggest that KASH5 connects the telomere-associated SUN1 protein to the cytoplasmic force-generating mechanism involved in meiotic chromosome movement.

evidence.reference_title: The KASH5 protein involved in meiotic chromosomal movements is a novel dynein activating adaptor.
evidence.snippet: We show that the meiosis-specific nuclear-envelope protein KASH5 is a dynein activating adaptor: KASH5 directly binds dynein using a mechanism conserved among activating adaptors and converts dynein into a processive motor.

evidence.reference_title: The meiotic LINC complex component KASH5 is an activating adaptor for cytoplasmic dynein.
evidence.snippet: Altogether, we show that the transmembrane protein KASH5 is an activating adaptor for dynein and shed light on the hierarchy of assembly of KASH5-dynein-dynactin complexes.

evidence.reference_title: Kinesin drive meiotic chromosome dynamics via interaction with the KASH5-LINC complex.
evidence.snippet: Altogether, our findings identify kinesins, particularly KIF5B, as a previously unrecognized component of the force-generating machinery that drives chromosome movement during meiotic prophase I, acting through KASH5 as a specific nuclear membrane adaptor.
